status: citation adapter draft; no scientific approval
integration: rows[row.id].finding and rows[row.id].magnitude are ordered {text,sources} arrays. Concatenate text exactly to reconstruct existing fields. Pass as optional findingSentences and magnitudeSentences; do not replace canonical text/values.
assignmentPolicy: Explicit field-specific source assignments; not automatic copying of all row source IDs.
Pure corpus/editorial missingness and absence of a pooled estimate receive sources:[].
Mixed sentences retain citations for their source-backed content; correction/access/pending qualifiers are internal recorded state, not claims that a paper approves this edition.
Computational interpretation describes the observed study design; it does not transform model scores into human benefit.
Background-only book/review sentences preserve background provenance and never become primary results.

finding.text: COVID-OUT’s reported hazard ratio is provisional while an indexed correction remains unresolved; it is not treated as a settled efficacy conclusion.
ACTIV-6’s secondary diagnosis estimate favored metformin but its interval included no difference.

magnitude.text: COVID-OUT: source-reported hazard ratio 0.59 (95% CI 0.39–0.89), provisional and on correction HOLD; cumulative-incidence percentages withheld.
ACTIV-6: risk difference −0.7 percentage points (95% credible interval −1.5 to 0.1).
No pooled estimate.

finding.text: ACTIV-6 did not meet its reported efficacy threshold for the primary long-term endpoint; its estimate remained compatible with a reduction or a small increase.

magnitude.text: Adjusted risk difference −0.8 percentage points (95% credible interval −2.2 to 0.6); raw events 33/1439 versus 46/1544.

finding.text: The South Korean trial did not show improved recovery with the studied metformin course; the abstract reports fewer recovered participants in the metformin arm than the placebo arm.

magnitude.text: Recovered: 84/132 (63.6%) with metformin versus 90/132 (68.2%) with placebo.
Between-group interval not extracted.

finding.text: STOP-PASC did not show a statistically significant between-group difference in its primary symptom-severity outcome.

magnitude.text: No numerical primary effect extracted.

finding.text: The secondary fatigue comparison did not show a clear advantage for nirmatrelvir–ritonavir; the confidence interval included differences in either direction.

magnitude.text: Adjusted between-group change difference 0.38 score points (95% CI −2.40 to 3.15).

finding.text: The RECOVER-VITAL abstract reports no statistically significant primary benefit in the selected symptom phenotypes.

finding.text: The pilot did not demonstrate a between-group clinical benefit on UPDRS total, despite improvement within the metformin arm.
